channel.title: Daybrief
channel.description: AI first. Everything else that matters, twice a day.

item.title: DeepSeek, MiniMax win approval to deploy models overseas, state media says
item.description: Chinese state media says DeepSeek and MiniMax completed export registration and won approval to open-source and deploy their AI models overseas. The report follows Beijing's recent move to tighten oversight of AI tech transfers. Why it matters: Shows how China's rules are shaping which homegrown AI models can reach global markets.

item.title: SK Hynix puts US IPO of chip unit Solidigm on hold after Seoul authorities raise concerns
item.description: SK Hynix has halted a planned US IPO of its Solidigm chip unit, citing market conditions, after Seoul authorities raised concerns. The listing was meant to fund a new US factory, and the company will keep exploring funding options. Why it matters: Shows how Seoul's scrutiny of deals can shape listings by major chipmakers that serve AI data-centre demand.

item.title: Ambani's US$3.2 billion Jio Indian IPO lures investors as bids surge on final day
item.description: Subscriptions for Jio Platforms' US$3.2 billion IPO surged on the final day of bidding, with public demand above seven times the shares on offer. It is India's largest ever IPO and a test of investor appetite for large listings. Why it matters: Tests whether investors will back big listings while AI-linked stocks face more scrutiny; Jio serves over 500 million users.

item.title: China APT Uses AI Pentest Tool Artex in ConnectWise Attacks
item.description: Microsoft says China-linked Storm-0940 used the open-source AI penetration-testing framework Artex to automate intrusions into ConnectWise customers' environments. The campaign targeted hundreds of organizations, and ConnectWise suspended several services in response. Why it matters: Shows state hackers adapting open-source AI pentesting tools to automate attacks at scale, relevant to cybersecurity defenders.

item.title: HSBC launches its first stablecoin for payments in Hong Kong
item.description: HSBC is rolling out RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, to more than 3.3 million PayMe users for payments. Users will be able to use it at more than 100,000 merchants; tokenized investment subscriptions are planned. Why it matters: Shows a major bank bringing stablecoins into everyday retail payments, relevant to fintech and markets watchers.

item.title: Sources: Anthropic and London-based PE firm Hg agree to launch a consultancy by the end of 2026 to embed AI consultants and engineers into European businesses
item.description: Anthropic and London-based buyout firm Hg plan a consultancy, due by end of 2026, to embed AI consultants and engineers in European businesses.

item.title: Google's Agent Compute Engine gives every Gemini agent its own hardware-isolated micro virtual machine
item.description: Google announced Agent Compute Engine, giving each AI agent its own hardware-isolated microVM; it powers Gemini and opens for preview in coming months.

item.title: Anthropic says it partnered with Theorem to use Claude to formally prove security properties at the assembly level across 100+ real-world open-source libraries
item.description: Anthropic and Theorem used Claude to formally prove security properties at assembly level in over 100 open-source libraries.

item.title: OpenAI lowers valuation target, raises up to $30 billion
item.description: OpenAI is closing in on a funding round of up to $30 billion at a lowered valuation target of $1.25 trillion, down from $1.4 trillion.

item.title: aiNTEL Launches Agentic Investigator, Giving Bank Financial Crime Teams a Complete Case in Hours, Not Days
Anticipating Social Consequences with Distributional World Models
item.description: A 4B model that predicts several possible consequences, with probabilities, for each candidate action performs best on 13 of 15 metrics.

item.title: Unified Trajectory and 3D Pose Forecasting for Multi-Agent Sports Analysis
item.description: A unified trajectory and 3D pose forecasting model improves over prior joint methods on WorldPose and 3DPW, with the largest gains in pose accuracy.

item.title: Termi Protocol
item.description: Termi shows real coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex working in a 3D room, with file reads, commands and edits visible live.

item.title: The same AI request emits 8.5 times more CO2 in Texas than in Sweden
item.description: Berget AI's open-source method estimates the same AI request emits 8.5 times more CO2 in Texas than in Sweden.

item.title: Qwen's Jiang Guanjun: A Personal Agent Technology Framework Requires Coordinated Progress in Models, Memory, and Ecosystem
AI Agents Are Rewriting the Value of CPUs: When Tokens Become Actions, Compute Competition Is No Longer Just About GPUs
Asia-Pacific AI agent market to surge 14-fold to US$11.2 billion by 2030, Omdia says
item.description: Omdia forecasts the AI agent software market across Asia, Australia and New Zealand will reach US$11.2 billion by 2030, up from US$782 million this year.

item.title: Incus 7.0.0 before 7.0.2 and 7.1.0 before 7.5.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows clients…
item.description: Certain Incus versions contain a path traversal flaw that lets clients who can create instances write files on the host.

item.title: Improper authentication in AAD App Proxy allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network
item.description: An improper authentication flaw in AAD App Proxy lets an unauthorized attacker elevate privileges over a network.

item.title: Attackers Exploit Third VeloCloud Orchestrator Zero-Day in Four Months
item.description: Arista patched an exploited zero-day, CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 9.9), a SQL injection in VeloCloud Orchestrator that lets authenticated users gain operator privileges.

item.title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
item.description: Until August 18 releases, the x402 SDKs' default client had no spending limit, so malicious APIs could get agents to sign payments for their full balance.

item.title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
item.description: Imperva researchers showed crafted Brotli data can make an official Node.js 24.22.0 Linux arm64 build run attacker-supplied code (CVE-2026-111497).

item.title: 11 Million Impacted by Capcom Data Breach
item.description: Capcom disclosed a breach of its CAPCOM ID service, with 11,774,247 email addresses stolen and passwords changed for 196 accounts.

item.title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware
item.description: Attackers compromised LiteLLM's release pipeline and published version 1.107.0 to PyPI and Docker with malware that steals credentials and loads remote-code execution tools.

item.title: Earnings flood, Fed meeting pose pivotal tests for rickety AI market rally
item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 23 : US stock investors face a pivotal week, with corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting both posing critical tests…

item.title: Nvidia's Huang heads to Kazakhstan for the first time — and he's not the only one with big plans
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, on his first visit to Kazakhstan, said the country could become an AI computing hub serving Europe, citing its energy resources and data center plans.

item.title: SK Hynix abandons plan for US unit's IPO, citing market volatility
item.description: SK Hynix has dropped plans for a New York IPO of its US unit after Korean regulators said it would breach a duplicate listing ban.

item.title: Malaysia, Thailand join Singapore’s cross-border stablecoin push
item.description: Bank Negara Malaysia and Bank of Thailand joined Singapore's BLOOM initiative, which aims to cut cross-border payment costs using stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

item.title: Singapore shares edge higher despite losses in local banks; STI up 0.1%
item.description: Singapore shares ended higher on Oct 23 as the STI gained 0.1% to 5,422.16, with CapitaLand Investment leading gainers.

item.title: Geely Auto, a key BYD rival, primed to re-enter Singapore market
item.description: Geely Auto is reportedly appointing an agent in Singapore and has held talks with major local automotive groups about a return.

item.title: Nvidia funds European startups. They spend it on Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang loves a European shopping spree.

item.title: Oslo tech struggles to break out of Stockholm's shadow
item.description: In a packed, mood-lit room in the centre of Oslo, the energy is buzzing.

item.title: SK Group’s data centre arm in talks to fund US$350 billion AI buildout
item.description: This involves a plan to develop 15GW of capacity in South Korea by 2030 SK HYPER is in talks with big tech firms and financial investors to secure funding for…

item.title: Japan to simulate cyberattacks with AI after PHP flaws
item.description: In Japan, SoftBank said it was suspending its emergency mobile alert system for maintenance to address a PHP vulnerability.

item.title: AI companies say they want to give billions away. Will they actually do it?
item.description: Some of Silicon Valley’s biggest names are digging deep into their pockets. Elon Musk has promised to give every child in America a share in SpaceX next year.

item.title: Series SEA: Who’s investing in the region’s education startups?
item.description: We've compiled a list of investors that are pouring money into Southeast Asia’s education startups.

item.title: Singapore’s core inflation eases to 2% in September on lower services, retail prices
item.description: Singapore's core inflation eased to 2% in September from 2.2% in August, driven by lower services and retail prices, official figures show.

item.title: OCBC Bank’s mobile, internet banking services restored after disruption: Spokesperson
item.description: OCBC's mobile and internet banking services were restored after an afternoon disruption on Oct 23, the bank said.

item.title: Singapore Exchange CEO signals succession planning as contract nears end in 2027
item.description: SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye said succession planning has begun, but no departure date is set; his contract runs to mid-July 2027.

item.title: Asian shares wobble as tech rout boosts bonds, dents rate hike bets
item.description: Asian shares fell on Oct 23 as concerns over AI's funding needs hit tech, driving investors into sovereign bonds.

item.title: The Mother Load: What 5 conversations reveal about modern motherhood in Singapore
item.description: The Straits Times' five-part podcast series The Mother Load explores maternal mental health, caregiving, parenting anxiety, working motherhood and fertility in Singapore.

item.title: [AINews] Black October
item.description: AINews calls 'Black October' a cluster of critical disclosures and breaches over about 48 hours, including an unauthenticated PHP remote code execution flaw.

item.title: Sources: OpenAI nears an up to $30B round led by investors from the UAE and Coatue at a $1.25T pre-money valuation, as an "opportunistic" bridge ahead of an IPO
item.description: OpenAI is nearing a round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, led by UAE investors and Coatue. It is meant to bridge the company to a 2027 IPO. Why it matters: Shows how investors value the AI giant ahead of its potential IPO, with UAE investors leading the round.

item.title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
item.description: Anthropic is donating its Agent Skills open standard to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. Anthropic says 70+ platforms have already integrated it. Why it matters: Puts a shared standard for giving AI agents specialized workflows under neutral, community-driven governance.

item.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end sharply lower as revived AI doubts ignite tech selloff
item.description: AI generated NEW YORK - US stocks tumbled on Oct 22 and the Nasdaq posted its steepest daily drop since June as a batch of high-profile earnings reports ignited fresh fears about the AI spending race. Why it matters: Shows how sensitive markets are to AI spending; the chip index has lost about a quarter since its June record.

item.title: 1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
item.description: Password manager 1Password launched 1Password for Agents, which lets AI agents log into users' personal accounts without the agent ever having access to their credentials. A unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent's identity. Why it matters: Addresses growing concern over AI agents holding access to personal accounts; 1Password reports $500M in ARR.

item.title: Arista patches new VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks
item.description: Arista released patches for an actively exploited SQL injection zero-day in VeloCloud Orchestrator on-prem deployments. Anyone able to log in, even with a read-only customer account, can gain operator privileges. Why it matters: Attacks are already underway against a critical-severity flaw in a central SD-WAN management system, tracked as CVE-2026-114625.

item.title: Someone hacked the Switch 2 by using an old game and AI
item.description: A modder jailbroke the Nintendo Switch 2 using a software-only, tethered exploit that OpenAI's Codex helped create.

item.title: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise
item.description: Microsoft says China-aligned hackers breached ConnectWise's cloud backup service and used AI agents to hack into about 2,250 organizations.

item.title: Sources: SoftBank's SB Energy is considering going public as soon as December or waiting until 2027, as it closely watches Anthropic's IPO, expected in November
item.description: SoftBank's SB Energy is considering an IPO as soon as December or waiting until 2027, while watching Anthropic's IPO expected in November.

item.title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
item.description: Canva launched Canva Craft, its first AI image model, which plans a design before generating the image and produces images up to 2K resolution.

item.title: Rivian buys world model startup to accelerate self-driving ambitions
item.description: Rivian acquired Third Dimension, a UK startup using AI to turn images and videos into 3D worlds for self-driving development.

item.title: How to Read Data into GPU Memory in Python with NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage
item.description: This guide shows how to use NVIDIA KvikIO, a Python library, to read data directly into GPU memory with GPUDirect Storage.

item.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
item.description: Microsoft and Hugging Face describe ThinkingBox-Training, which uses database checks as rewards, lifting one model's average task success from 51.70% to 60.78%.

item.title: OpenShell – A safe, private runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents
item.description: OpenShell is a runtime that runs AI agents in isolated sandboxes, enforcing declared policies on file access, system calls, and network connections.

item.title: Deploy AI in a HIPAA-eligible environment with Amazon Quick
item.description: A post explains that Amazon Quick is HIPAA-eligible but eligibility is not compliance, and outlines how to deploy AI agents in healthcare settings.

item.title: Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: A post shows how to stream each agent sentence to a Kokoro-82M speech model on SageMaker AI, so audio starts before the reply is done.

item.title: Why AI Compute Comes in Rectangles — Erik Bernhardsson, Modal CEO
item.description: In an interview, Modal's CEO explains the economics of elastic GPU compute, noting demand rarely matches the fixed capacity contracts used to buy it.

item.title: AI and the Enclosure of the Scientific Commons
item.description: This paper argues that AI can enable a previously infeasible enclosure of the scientific literature, which it calls an information commons.

item.title: Wasmtime 39.0.0 before 48.0.4 and 49.0.0 before 49.0.2 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability that…
item.description: Wasmtime 39.0.0 to before 48.0.4, and 49.0.0 to before 49.0.2, have a stack overflow that can crash the host or let attackers escape the sandbox.
